text: A home for the albums you care about, sorted your way, that opens each one in the service you listen with. Tonaris keeps your albums: the ones you love, the ones you mean to hear, and the ones you want to come back to. You sort them the way you think about music. When you want to listen, Tonaris opens the album in Spotify, Apple Music, Qobuz, Tidal or YouTube Music. On a computer: your folders and lists on the left, a list's albums in the middle, one album open on the right.

heading: Five ideas
text: Everything in Tonaris builds on these. ### Albums Your collection is made of albums, not songs. Each album is in it once, with its title, artist, year and cover. You don't type these: paste a link to the album, and Tonaris fills them in. ### Lists A list is a set of albums, like a playlist of albums: Late night, To listen, Best of 1974. An album can be in as many lists as you like. It's still one album, so when you fix its year, every list shows the new year. ### Folders Folders hold lists, and other folders, many levels deep. A folder Moods can hold the lists Late night and Rainy Sundays, and a folder Jazz can hold a folder for each decade. ### Unsorted An album in no list waits in Unsorted. Nothing gets lost: take an album out of its last list, and that's where it goes. ### Your streaming services Tonaris doesn't play music. Each album keeps a link to each service it's on, and opens there, in the service's web page or its app.

heading: What else it does
text: Share a folder or a list with people you invite, to look or to help build it, or with anyone who has its link. Add your own fields to albums: a rating, the format you own it on, where you bought it, anything. Let an AI assistant help. Claude, ChatGPT and Codex can look through your collection and change it, and ask you first before deleting anything. Keep everything in step. Each change is saved as you make it and shows on every device you're signed in on. Take your data with you. Export the whole collection whenever you like. Use the keyboard. Almost everything has a key: press ? in Tonaris to see them all. On a phone, you can look through your collection, search it and open albums. Adding and organizing need a computer. Ready? Your first ten minutes walks you through your first album and your first list.

text: Make a list, add an album to it from a link, and play it in your streaming service. Do this on a computer: adding albums and making lists need one. You'll need a link to an album from Spotify, Apple Music, Qobuz, Tidal or YouTube Music.

heading: 1. Make a list
text: In the sidebar, choose + beside Collection, then New list. Or press N. Type a name, such as Late night, and press Enter. Your new list shows in the sidebar. Choose it to open it: it's empty for now.

heading: 2. Copy an album's link
text: In your streaming app or on its website, find an album you like. Open its share menu and copy the album's link. A link to one of its songs works too: Tonaris finds the album the song is on.

heading: 3. Add the album
keys: C cmd command ctrl control V
text: In Tonaris, with your new list open, choose Add album in the sidebar. Or press C. Paste the link into Links. You can paste several, one per line. List already says your new list. Choose Add. Add albums takes links from any of the five services, and puts the albums in the list you choose. Tonaris looks the album up and fills in its title, artist, year and cover. If it isn't sure which album you mean, it asks. Faster: with a list open, just paste. Press ⌘ V while no text field is selected and no album is open on the right, and the album goes into that list.

heading: 4. Play it
text: Each album shows the services it has links for. Choose one, such as Spotify, to open the album there. When an album has more links than fit, +2 or similar opens the rest. Or select the album and press O for Open in…, which lists them all. Open in… lists every service the album has a link for.

heading: 5. Make it yours
text: In Settings, then Preferences: Open links in: choose App to open albums in your streaming apps rather than their web pages. Streaming services: turn off the services you don't use, and put the ones you use most first. To get to Settings, choose your name at the top of the sidebar, then Settings. Or press G then S.

heading: Where to go next
text: Put the same album in more lists, and sort lists into folders. Share a list with a friend. Install Tonaris as an app, on your computer or your phone. Press ? to see every key Tonaris has.

heading: Joining Tonaris
text: Tonaris is invitation-only for now. When you're invited, an email arrives with a link to join. Open the link in the email. The page shows the address the invitation is for. Choose Continue. Tonaris emails that address a 6-digit code. Type the code, or open the link in that email. Choose a display name, the name the people you share with will see. You can skip it and choose one later. Your collection opens, empty and ready for your first album. Joining means you agree to the terms of use and the privacy notice.

heading: Signing in
text: Sign in asks for your email, then for the code Tonaris sends to it. Go to tonaris.app/sign-in, type your email, and choose Continue. Type the 6-digit code from the email, or open the link in it. A code works for 10 minutes. If the email hasn't arrived, look in your spam folder. After 30 seconds you can ask for a new code. Opened the link on another phone or computer? Tonaris asks there whether to sign in on that device, so a link opened by mistake signs nobody in. You stay signed in on each device for 30 days after you last used Tonaris there.

heading: Signing in with a passkey
text: A passkey lets your phone or computer sign you in with your face, fingerprint or screen lock, without an email. Sign in with a code first. Then choose your name at the top of the sidebar, then Settings, then Account. Choose Add a passkey and follow what your device asks. Next time, choose Sign in with a passkey on the sign-in page. Your browser may also offer the passkey when you select the email field.

heading: Signing out
text: Choose your name at the top of the sidebar, then Sign out. If some of your changes haven't been saved yet, Tonaris asks before it signs you out, so nothing is lost by accident.

heading: Lost access to your email?
text: If you can't get email at your sign-in address any more, the Tonaris creator can move your account to a new address. Your collection, sharing and settings stay as they are. Here's what to do.

heading: Remove the app

Chrome or Edge on a computer: in the Tonaris window, open the menu, then choose Uninstall Tonaris (in Edge, App settings has it too). Safari on a Mac: remove Tonaris from your Dock, and drag it from the Applications folder in your home folder to the Bin. iPhone or iPad: touch and hold the Tonaris icon, then tap Remove App, then Delete. Android: touch and hold the Tonaris icon, then tap Uninstall or Remove.

heading: MusicBrainz and the Cover Art Archive
text: MusicBrainz is an open music encyclopedia that anyone can edit. Tonaris takes the album's title, artist, year and release type from it, and, for a live album, when it was recorded. The Cover Art Archive holds covers that MusicBrainz's community uploads. Tonaris uses the album's front cover, when there is one. Tonaris doesn't copy details from the streaming services. One exception: when MusicBrainz doesn't have an album from an Apple Music link, the album form offers Apple's title, artist and year for you to check. An album without a cover shows its first letter instead. You can add a cover yourself.

heading: Albums, not editions
text: Tonaris keeps albums, not editions. A remaster, a deluxe edition or a vinyl reissue is the same album as the original. Whichever edition your link is for, Tonaris saves the album with its original title and the year it first came out. So each album is in your collection once. A link to another edition of an album you have goes to that album. Two different albums with the same title stay apart.

heading: Which year an album shows
text: Most albums show the year they first came out, from their earliest release. Live albums show when they were recorded, after "rec.": rec. 1998, or rec. 1975–1985 for a recording made over several years. A live album whose recording year isn't known shows its release year, with a small calendar mark. Point to the mark to read "Recording year unknown — sorted by release year". Sorting by year uses the year the album shows. Every album has a year: when MusicBrainz doesn't know it, Tonaris asks you for it.

heading: Release types
text: An album's release type is Album, EP, Single or Compilation, from MusicBrainz. Live is separate, so an album can be a live compilation. When MusicBrainz doesn't say, the type is Unknown. When albums show as covers, a small label in a cover's top-left corner says EP, Single, Compilation or Live. A studio album has no label. In rows, the type has a column of its own. Labels show what isn't a plain studio album. Live albums show when they were recorded.

heading: Your edits stay
text: Tonaris fills in only what's missing. It never changes a value an album already has, whether you typed it or it came from MusicBrainz. When you add a link for an album you already have, Tonaris may fill a gap, such as a missing cover, and leaves everything else as it is. So if you change an album's year or type, it stays as you set it. MusicBrainz has no say over it after that.

Custom fields add what matters to you: a rating, the formats you own it on, when you bought it. You make a field once, then use it on any album you like.

heading: Make a field
keys: G S cmd command ctrl control Enter
text: Choose your name at the top of the sidebar, then Settings. Or press G then S. Choose Custom fields, then New field. Type a Name, such as Rating, and choose a Type. For Single choice or Multiple choice, type the Options, one in each box. Add option adds a box. Choose Create field, or press ⌘ Enter. The new field is on no album yet. You can also make one from an album, as below. Settings → Custom fields lists your fields and how many albums use each.

heading: The six types
text: Type What it holds For example Text Any words Notes: "Signed copy, Lisbon" Number A number Plays: 12 Date A date Bought: 2026-03-14 Yes/no Yes or No Heard live: Yes Single choice One of the options you set Rating: ★★★★ Multiple choice Any of the options you set Format: Vinyl, CD Type a date as year, month and day, such as 2026-03-14, or pick it from the calendar.

heading: Use a field on an album
text: Open the album in the album panel, and switch to Editing mode with E. Under Custom fields, choose Add field, then the field. Create field… makes a new field and adds it. Fill it in: type the text, number or date and press Enter, or choose Yes, No or an option. A choice saves as you make it. Typed values save when you press Enter or move on, and Esc puts back what was there. The values belong to the album, so they're the same in every list it's in. In Editing mode, the album panel's fields can be filled in.

heading: Empty is not the same as not added
text: A field you add to an album and leave empty shows Empty, or — for Yes/no. That's different from a field the album doesn't have, and different from 0 or No. Tonaris never fills in a value for you. So Rating added but empty can mean "not rated yet", and no Rating at all, "not one I rate". To take a field off an album, choose × next to it in Editing mode. Its value goes with it, and Undo brings both back. Add the field again later, and it starts empty.

heading: Limits
text: Up to 50 fields. Up to 100 options in each choice field. Up to 2,000 characters in a text value. Two fields can't have the same name, and two options in one field can't have the same name, even with different capital letters. Search doesn't look in custom fields: it finds albums by their title and artist.

heading: What the people you share with see
text: When you share a folder or list, the fields its albums use are shared with it, with their values. Fields that none of those albums use stay private, and so do options none of them chose. People who can edit your folder or list see all your fields and all their options, so they can fill them in on its albums. Only you can make, rename or delete fields and options. See Change or remove a field. On a phone, an album's details show its fields and values. Making fields and filling them in needs a computer.

heading: Rename a field
text: Choose the field's name to open it. Change its Name and press Enter. Esc puts back the old name. The new name shows on every album at once, in Trash too, and every value stays as it was. Like a new field, it can't take the name of another of your fields.

heading: Change its type
text: You can change a field's Type only while no album uses it: not an album in Trash, and not an album with the field added but empty. When an album does, the Type is locked, with a line such as "Used by 3 albums. Create a new field of the type you need instead." and a Create new field button. Why: a new type would mean turning every value into something else, such as dates into numbers. Tonaris never changes or throws away your values to make that possible. So make a new field of the type you need, fill it in, then delete the old one. A field's type is locked while any album uses it. While no album uses it: Between Single choice and Multiple choice, the options stay as they are. From a choice type to any other type, the options go. Tonaris lists them first and changes the type only when you choose Change type. Keep options leaves it as it was. Changing back later doesn't bring the options back.

heading: Change the options
text: Rename an option: change its text and press Enter. Every album that chose it shows the new name. Add an option: type it in the New option box and press Enter, or choose Add option. It goes at the end. Remove an option: choose × next to it. If no album chose it, it goes at once. If any album chose the option, Tonaris asks first, in a message such as "Remove option 'Cassette'?" with how many albums chose it. Confirm with Remove from 3 albums, or whatever number it shows. Removing it clears it from those albums, in Trash too. A single choice becomes empty, and a multiple choice keeps its other options. The field stays on those albums. Removing an option that albums chose can't be undone. Adding an option with the same name later makes a new one that no album has chosen.

heading: Delete a field
text: Choose the field's name to open it. Choose Delete field. Tonaris shows what goes: the field, its options, and how many albums have it. Choose Delete field again to confirm. Tonaris always asks, even when no album uses the field. Deleting a field takes it and its values off every album, in Trash too. It can't be undone: the field doesn't go to Trash, and getting an album back from Trash doesn't bring the field back. You can then make a new field with the same name. It starts on no album.

text: Choose Share on a folder or list, then invite people by email or turn on its link. Sharing happens in the sharing dialog. There you invite people, choose what each one can do, and turn the link on or off.

heading: Open the sharing dialog
text: Open the folder or list you want to share. Choose Share at the top of the page, or press ⇧ S. From the sidebar: choose ⋯ beside a folder or list, or press ⇧ F10 on it, then choose Share…. The dialog starts by saying what sharing means: a folder includes everything inside it, now and in the future, and people who can edit can add, change, move and delete what's inside. Read it before you share.

heading: Add a display name first
text: People you share with see your display name, not your email. If you don't have one yet, the dialog asks for it under Add a display name to share. Type a name and choose Save. While you share anything, you can change your name but not remove it.

heading: Invite people
text: Choose Can view or Can edit in the menu beside Invite by name or email…. Type the person's email address. Choose Invite, or press Enter. When you select the field, your people show under it, the most recent first. Type part of a name to find someone else. Choose a person, or move to them with ↑ and ↓ and press Enter, to invite them at once with the role beside the field. The person needs a Tonaris account with that email. If no account uses it, the dialog says so and keeps what you typed, so you can fix a typo or share a link instead. Each person has a row with their status and what they can do.

heading: Who has access
text: Each person you invite gets a row: their name, their email, then Pending until they accept, and Accepted after. A pending row also says how its email is doing: sending…, sent, email failed or email not confirmed. For the last two, choose Resend. The invitation is saved either way, and the person also finds it in Tonaris. The email says who invited them, to which folder or list, and whether to view or to edit. Its link works only for them: forwarding it gives no one access. When a folder above is shared too, the dialog says so, for example Also visible through "Jazz": 1 person. Choose the folder's name to open its sharing dialog.

heading: Share a link
text: Turn on Link sharing. Choose Copy. The button then says Copied. Paste the link where you like: a message, an email, a post. Anyone with the link can view the folder or list and send the link on. It's the same link each time you open the dialog. A link only lets people view: to let someone edit, invite them.

heading: See what you share
text: In the sidebar and on folder pages, a shared folder or list has a small mark after its name: people for invitations, a chain link for a link, or both. A paler mark means it's shared through a folder above. Sharing needs a connection. Offline, the dialog says "You're offline. Sharing waits until you're back." Share isn't on a phone. Share from a computer.

text: In the sharing dialog, change what someone can do, remove their access, or turn the link off. Each change works at once. Each change here is made in the sharing dialog: open the folder or list, then choose Share, or press ⇧ S. It saves at once, and the people it affects see the change straight away.

heading: Change what someone can do
text: In the person's row, open the menu that says Can view or Can edit. Choose the other one. The person doesn't need to accept again. Changed to Can view, they can't make any more changes, and a share they have open turns view-only. A row may say Also editable through "Jazz". That person can edit a folder above, so they can edit this one too, whatever its row says. To change that, change their role in the folder above.

heading: Remove someone's access
text: Choose ⋯ at the end of the person's row. Choose Remove access. It works on pending and accepted invitations, and it doesn't ask first. The person can no longer open the folder or list, and in their Shared with me it shows as "No longer available". If they also have the link, the link still works for them: turn it off too. To share with them again, invite them again.

heading: Turn the link off
text: Turn off Link sharing. Tonaris asks first. Choose Turn off. The link stops working for good, for everyone who has it. Turning link sharing on again makes a new, different link: the old one never works again. People who kept the old link in their Shared with me see it as "No longer available" until they open the new link and add it again. A link you turn off never works again.

heading: Stop sharing with one person everywhere
text: To end everything you share with someone in one step, open their page in People and choose Stop sharing with and their name, such as Stop sharing with Sam…. People explains how.

heading: What stopping doesn't change
text: What people who could edit added or changed stays in your collection. What they share with you stays shared. Stopping can't take back copies. Anyone who could open a folder or list may have copied it into their own collection, and that copy stays theirs.

heading: Moving into or out of a shared folder
text: Move a folder or list into a shared folder, and the people and the link of that folder see it too. Move it out, and the people who saw it only through that folder no longer see it. Its own sharing goes with it. If you shared the list itself, by invitation or by link, that still works after the move.

page: Moving or deleting what you share
heading: Tonaris shows you first
text: When you move a folder or list with Move to… (press M) or by dragging it onto a folder in the sidebar, Tonaris shows what the move would change: Newly visible to … : who would start seeing it. No longer visible through a folder: who would stop seeing it, and through which folder they saw it. Still shared directly with … : its own sharing, which stays. Sharing unchanged: nobody gains or loses it. People who haven't accepted yet show with "(invited)". If someone can still see it another way, Tonaris doesn't say they lose it. When a move changes who can see it, Tonaris asks before moving, such as "Move 'To listen' to 'Jazz'?". Choose Move to go ahead, or Cancel to leave it where it is. A move that changes nothing happens at once. A move that changes who can see something waits for you to confirm it.

page: Moving or deleting what you share
heading: Deleting something you share
text: While a folder or list is in Trash, nobody it's shared with can open it, by invitation or by link. Its invitations and its link are kept, not ended. When you delete a folder, with Delete… in its ⋯ menu in the sidebar or by pressing ⌫, Tonaris asks first. When the folder, something in it, or a folder above it is shared, the question says that its people and links can't open it while it's in Trash, and that restoring it gives them access again. A list goes to Trash at once, with Undo, and its sharing pauses the same way. Meanwhile, people see "No longer available" in Tonaris. A link says "This link isn't available. Ask the person who shared it for a new one." After 30 days in Trash, it's deleted for good, and its sharing ends.

page: Moving or deleting what you share
heading: Restoring it
text: Restoring it in Trash, with Restore or by pressing R, turns its sharing back on: accepted invitations, and the link if you didn't turn it off, work again. Invitations nobody answered yet are still waiting. Access you removed, and a link you turned off, while it was in Trash stay that way. When restoring would let anyone see it, Tonaris asks first, such as "Restore 'Late night'?" with "Once it's back, others can see it." and who. Choose Restore. Undo right after a deletion doesn't ask. Get something back from Trash explains restoring.

text: Accept an invitation, and the folder or list shows in Shared with me, always up to date. A shared link opens without an account. Someone can share a folder or list with you by inviting you, or by sending you its link.

heading: Answer an invitation
text: You hear about an invitation in an email, such as "Robin invited you to view "Late night" on Tonaris", and in Tonaris: a notice if it's open, and Invitations in the sidebar while any wait for you. Choose Invitations in the sidebar, or View in the notice, or open the link in the email. Choose Accept or Decline. Each invitation says who it's from, the folder or list, the date, and "to edit" when you're invited to edit. Nothing is shared with you until you accept. Accepting puts it in Shared with me. The email's link works only when you're signed in with the address it was sent to. An invitation that was withdrawn, or that you declined, says "This invitation is no longer available."

heading: Shared with me

text: Shared with me in the sidebar lists what's shared with you, each with its owner's name, such as Summer 2026 · Mira. A pencil after it means you can edit it. Choose Shared with me itself to see them all, by owner, each marked "by invitation" or "from a link". A shared folder or list opens with "View only · Shared by Mira" at the top, or "Can edit" when you can edit it. Choose it to see more about Mira. What you see is always up to date: when Mira adds an album, it shows without reloading. How it looks is up to you. Choose View, or press V, to sort, group, or show covers. heading: Copy one into your collection
text: On a computer, choose Copy to my collection… at the top of a shared folder or list. Choose where the copy goes, check its name, and choose Copy. The copy is yours: what's inside now, with no link to the original. Albums you already have join its lists instead of being copied twice. If the copy would go over a limit, nothing is copied, and Tonaris says which limit.

heading: Open a shared link
text: A link opens in any browser, without an account. You see the folder or list, who shared it, and the albums with their streaming links. You can sort it and switch between rows and a grid, for this visit only. When you're signed in to Tonaris, the page offers Add to Shared with me. Choose it to keep the share; it then says In Shared with me. Opening a link on its own adds nothing. A link that says "This link isn't available. Ask the person who shared it for a new one." was turned off, or what it shares is in Trash.

heading: Leave or remove a share
text: On the Shared with me page: For one from an invitation, choose Leave share…, then Leave. To come back, you'd need a new invitation. For one from a link, choose Remove from Shared with me. Nothing changes for the owner or anyone else.

heading: No longer available
text: When the owner stops sharing with you, turns off the link you kept, or moves it to Trash, it shows dimmed as "No longer available". Choose Remove to take it off your list. One in Trash comes back if the owner restores it. On a phone, switch the Collection screen to Shared: your invitations, People and what's shared with you are there. Copying needs a computer.

text: When someone lets you edit, you change their folder or list as they would, inside it only. Everything you add stays in their collection. When someone invites you with Can edit, you help build their folder or list. What you add or change is saved in their collection, and they see it at once, as does everyone they share it with. page: Editing someone else's folder or list
heading: How you know you can edit
text: The invitation, and its email, say "to edit". In Shared with me it says "you can edit", and the sidebar shows a pencil after its name. At the top of the folder or list: "Can edit · Shared by" and the owner's name. If you can edit a folder, you can edit everything inside it.

page: Editing someone else's folder or list
heading: Start editing
text: Open the folder or list from Shared with me in the sidebar. Switch to Edit, or press E. The sidebar keeps showing your own collection. Your sort, grouping and layout of the share are your own. Editing a share works as in your own collection, inside the share.

page: Editing someone else's folder or list
heading: What you can do
text: Inside the share you can: Make lists and folders: choose New list or New folder at the top of a folder, or press N or ⇧ N. Rename folders and lists: choose Rename at the top, or press F2. You can also give them descriptions, colors and icons. Move them to other folders in the share: press M for Move to…. Add albums to its lists, from links or by hand: choose Add album in the sidebar, or press C, and pick one of the share's lists. Change an album's details, cover, links and custom-field values. You see all the owner's fields. The change shows wherever the album is in their collection. Take albums out of its lists, and delete folders, lists and albums.

page: Editing someone else's folder or list
heading: What stays with the owner
text: The shared folder or list itself. You can rename it, describe it, and set its color and icon, but not move or delete it. Where things go. Nothing moves out of the share, to the top of their collection, or into another share. Move to… offers only the share's folders. Custom fields. You fill them in, but can't add, rename or delete fields or their choices. Sharing. You can't invite people or turn on a link, and you don't see who else has access. Their Trash and their settings.

text: Deleting an album (press ⌘ ⌫) takes it out of every list in the share. Tonaris asks first, such as "Delete 'Field Notes' from 'Jazz'?". If the owner has the album in other lists, it stays there. If not, it goes to their Trash. Deleting a list (press ⌫) moves it to the owner's Trash, with Undo right after. A folder asks first. Once it's in their Trash, only the owner can restore it.

page: Editing someone else's folder or list
heading: When you can no longer edit
text: If the owner changes you to Can view, the share turns view-only. If they remove your access, it says it's no longer available. Changes not saved by then are reported, such as "2 changes weren't saved". What you added before stays in the owner's collection.

page: Editing someone else's folder or list

text: An AI agent you connected with Manage collection can change the share as you can. One connected as Read-only can only read it. Accepting invitations and leaving shares happen in Tonaris itself. On a phone, a share you can edit opens view-only. Edit it on a computer.

text: Your people are everyone you've shared with by invitation, either way. The People page shows what you share with each of them, and what they share with you. heading: The People page
text: Choose People in the sidebar. Each person shows their avatar, their name, the email you typed for them, and what's shared each way, such as "You share 1 folder (1 to edit)" and "Shares 1 list with you". heading: A person's page
text: Choose a person to see: their About text and favorite albums, if they added them (see below); You share with them: each folder or list, whether they Can view or Can edit, and Pending or Accepted. On a computer, choosing one opens its sharing dialog; what they share with you: choosing one opens it, or its invitation while it waits for your answer. A person's page shows what's shared each way.

heading: Your profile
text: Your people see your About text and up to 4 favorite albums on your page in their People. They also see your About in the card that opens from "Shared by" on what you share. Anyone else, including people with a link, sees only your name and avatar. You add these in Settings: Your profile and who sees it.

heading: Suggestions when you invite
text: In the sharing dialog, your people show under the invite field, the 8 most recent first. Type part of a name or email to find the others. People already invited to that folder or list aren't shown. Someone who invited you shows by name only: you see their email only if you typed it yourself. When two people have the same name, each says what they share with you, such as Mira · shares "Summer 2026" with you.

heading: Stop sharing with someone
text: On the person's page, such as Sam's, choose Stop sharing with Sam…. Check the list of what Sam will lose, then choose Stop sharing with Sam. heading: Remove someone from People
text: On their page, choose Remove from People. They no longer show on the People page or in the invite field, and they no longer see your About or favorites. Nothing you share with them stops. They come back when one of you invites the other again. On a phone, find People on the Collection screen's Shared side. You can look at it there; stopping sharing and removing people need a computer.

heading: Take an album out of a list
text: Open the list and choose the album. In the album panel, under Lists, choose × beside the list's name. Or press ⌫. A notice says Removed from and the list's name, with Undo, which puts the album back. In a list you arranged by hand, it goes back at the end. heading: Delete a list
text: Open the list, or find it in the sidebar. Choose Delete list at the top of the list, or Delete… in the list's ⋯ menu in the sidebar. Or press ⌫. The list goes to Trash at once, and a notice says 1 list moved to Trash, with Undo. Its albums stay in your other lists. An album that was in no other list goes to the top of Unsorted.

heading: Delete a folder
text: Choose Delete folder at the top of the folder, or Delete… in its ⋯ menu. Or press ⌫. Tonaris asks first, naming the folder and what's inside it. Its albums stay in their other lists or in Unsorted. Choose the button that moves them, such as Move 1 folder and 2 lists to Trash. There is no Undo for a folder. To get it back, restore it from Trash.

heading: Delete an album from your collection

text: Choose the album. Choose Delete from collection…, the bin icon at the top of the album panel, beside its close button. Or press ⌘ ⌫. Tonaris names the lists the album leaves. Choose Move to Trash. The bin icon stays at the top of the panel, so it's in view however long the album's details are. To delete several albums, select them with X and choose Delete… in the bar under the albums. Deleting an album always asks first, and names the lists it leaves.

heading: What goes to Trash together
text: A folder goes to Trash with everything inside it, as one item. Restoring the folder brings all of it back. Something you deleted on its own stays on its own. If you delete a list and later its folder, restoring the folder leaves the list in Trash. Albums you delete together by selecting them each go to Trash on their own.

heading: What can't be undone

heading: How the keys work
keys: cmd command ctrl control K esc escape Enter G H question mark
text: Keys wait while you type. In a text field, and while a dialog or menu is open, the keys above do nothing, so you can type freely. Three work anyway: ⌘ K opens search, Esc closes or cancels, and ⌘ Enter sends a form. Two keys in a row. For keys such as G then H, press the first key, let go, then press the second within a second and a half. See them in Tonaris. Press ?, or choose your name at the top of the sidebar, then Keyboard shortcuts. Every command is in search too. Press ⌘ K and type a command's name, such as Add to list: it shows its key beside it. Type > first to see commands only. A few commands, such as Color…, Icon… and Move to position…, have no key, so you find them only there. Phones have no keys. On a phone, use the buttons at the top of each screen. To move through the sidebar and your albums by keyboard alone, see Move around with the keyboard.

text: Tonaris reads album and song links from Spotify, Apple Music, Qobuz, Tidal and YouTube Music. Playlists, artists and other services don't work. Copy a link from a service's Share menu, and paste it into Tonaris. A link to an album adds that album. A link to a song adds the album the song is on.

heading: The five services
text: Service Links that work Spotify Album and song links from open.spotify.com, short links from spotify.link, and spotify:album: and spotify:track: codes Apple Music Album and song links from music.apple.com Qobuz Album pages on qobuz.com, and album and track links from open.qobuz.com and play.qobuz.com Tidal Album and track links from tidal.com and listen.tidal.com YouTube Music Album links from YouTube Music's Share menu, and songs played inside an album Links can have extra parts, such as a country or ?si= at the end. Tonaris tidies each link before saving it, so two forms of the same link count as one.

heading: Songs from Tidal and Qobuz
text: Their song links don't say which album a song is on. So Tonaris asks you for the album's title, artist and year, and keeps the link with the album. See Add an album by hand.

heading: YouTube Music
text: On YouTube Music, an album is a special kind of playlist. To get a link that works: In YouTube Music, open the album. Copy its link from Share. A link to a song you play inside an album works too. A video on its own, or a playlist someone made, doesn't name an album, and Tonaris says so.

heading: What doesn't work
text: playlists, artist pages, podcasts and profiles; other services, such as Deezer, Bandcamp or Amazon Music; links with a part missing. Copy them again from the service. When Tonaris can't read a link, it says why. You can still add the album by hand.

heading: How links open
text: Each album keeps at most one link for each service. Opening one is always your choice: choose a service's name on the album, or select the album and choose Open in…, or press O. Tonaris never opens a service for you. Web page or app. In Settings, then Preferences, Open links in chooses Web page, the setting at the start, or App. App opens Spotify, Apple Music, Qobuz and Tidal in their apps, on every device you use. A service whose app isn't installed won't open. YouTube Music has no desktop app, so its links always open its web page. People who open your shared link without signing in get the web pages. More in Listen in your streaming service.

heading: At a limit
text: Only the new thing is refused, with a message that says why and what to do. Everything else keeps working: you can still open, edit, move, remove and share. At the album limit, a new album is refused. Getting an album back from Trash still works, and so does adding a link to an album you already have, since neither needs a new place. At the hourly limit on links, you can still add albums by hand, or try again later. What people add to a folder or list they can edit for you counts toward your limits, as it's in your collection.

heading: Trash counts
text: Albums, folders and lists in Trash count until they're deleted for good, by you or after 30 days. To make room now, delete them from Trash on a computer. Taking an album out of a list frees nothing: the album is still in your collection.

heading: See your usage
text: In Settings, then Data, Usage shows how many albums you have of the limit, how many of them are in Trash, and a bar for both. To get there, choose your name at the top of the sidebar, then Settings, or press G then S. Then choose Data. When you're close to the album limit, Add albums shows how many you've used, with links to Trash and to your usage.

text: What the words Tonaris uses mean, from album to passkey, each with the page that says more. The words below are the ones Tonaris shows on screen. Each one links to the page that says more.

heading: Your collection
text: Collection: everything you keep in Tonaris: your folders, lists and albums. It's at the top of the sidebar, and it's the first screen on a phone. Press G then H to go there. Your first ten minutes Album: one album, EP, single, live album or compilation, with its title, artist, year, cover and links. Each album is in your collection once, however many lists it's in. Add albums by pasting links List: a set of albums you put together, such as Late night or To listen. An album can be in as many lists as you like. Put albums in lists and take them out Folder: holds lists, and other folders, to keep them in order. A folder holds no albums of its own. Folders and lists Unsorted: where albums that are in no list wait. Take an album out of its last list, and it goes there; nothing is deleted. Press G then U. One album, many lists, and Unsorted Remove and delete: removing takes an album out of a list, and it stays in your collection. Deleting moves it to Trash. Remove, delete and undo Trash: keeps what you delete for 30 days, so you can get it back. After that, it's gone for good. Press G then T. Get something back from Trash Album panel: the panel that opens on the right when you select an album, with its details, links and fields. On a phone, an album opens in a sheet from the bottom instead. The album panel Viewing and Editing: the two modes on a computer. Viewing is for looking and listening; Editing lets you rename, fix details and rearrange. Press E to switch. Viewing and Editing Custom field: something you add to albums yourself, such as a rating, the format you own, or the day you bought it. Track anything with custom fields Release type: what kind of release an album is. A list can be grouped by it: Album, EP, Single, Live, Compilation and Unclassified. Covers or rows, sorting and grouping

text: Can view: a person you share with as Can view sees the folder or list, and can't change it. Share a folder or list Can edit: a person you share with as Can edit can also add albums, change them and arrange them. Your custom fields, sharing and Trash stay yours. Editing someone else's folder or list Link: a folder or list shared by link opens for anyone who has the link, without an account. Ways to share Guest: someone who opens a shared link without signing in. Guests can look and open albums, nothing more. Change or stop sharing Shared with me: the place in the sidebar for the folders and lists others share with you. When someone shares with you People: everyone you share with, and everyone who shares with you. People

text: Short answers to the questions people ask most, each with the page that says more.

heading: Is there a password?
text: No. Tonaris has no passwords. You sign in with a 6-digit code sent to your email, or with a passkey: your face, fingerprint or screen lock. Your sign-in email and passkeys

heading: What if my sign-in code doesn't arrive?
text: Look in your spam or junk folder, and check the email address you typed. After 30 seconds, you can ask for a new code; each code works for 10 minutes. Joining and signing in If you can't get email at that address any more, see Lost access to your email?

heading: Does Tonaris play music?
text: No. Tonaris keeps your albums and opens each one in the service you listen with: Spotify, Apple Music, Qobuz, Tidal or YouTube Music. Choose a service's name on an album, or press O for Open in…. Listen in your streaming service

heading: Can I import my Spotify library?
text: No. Tonaris doesn't connect to your streaming libraries, in either direction, and importing isn't planned. Instead, copy album links from your service and paste them into Add albums, up to 200 at once and 100 in an hour. An AI agent can also add albums from links. Add albums by pasting links

heading: Can I add songs or playlists?
text: Tonaris keeps albums, EPs, singles, live albums and compilations, not songs. A link to a song adds the album the song is on. Playlist links don't work: to keep a playlist's albums, make a list and add each album's link. Services and links Tonaris reads

heading: Why does an album show this year?
text: Tonaris shows the year the album first came out, not the year of the edition your link points to: a 2015 remaster of a 1972 album shows 1972. A live album shows the year it was recorded, after rec., when that's known. You can change the year in the album panel. Where album details come from

heading: Why is a cover missing?
text: Some albums have no cover where Tonaris looks them up. To add one, select the album and switch to Editing with E. Then choose Find beside Artwork URL to pick a cover, or paste an image's address there. Fix an album's details, cover and links

heading: Can I keep a vinyl and a CD edition apart?
text: Not as two albums. Tonaris keeps each album once, whichever edition a link points to, so a link to a deluxe edition adds the same album. To note what you own, add a custom field, such as a multiple-choice Format with Vinyl, CD and Cassette. Track anything with custom fields

heading: What is Unsorted?
text: Unsorted holds the albums that are in no list. An album you add without a list goes there, and so does one you take out of its last list. Put it in a list, and it leaves Unsorted. One album, many lists, and Unsorted

heading: How many albums can I keep?
text: 50,000, counting those in Trash. Settings, then Data shows how many you have. Limits

heading: Who can see my collection?
text: Only you, until you share. When you share a folder or list, the people you invite see it, and so does anyone with its link if you make one. AI agents you connect see your whole collection. The people you share with also see your profile. Ways to share

heading: Can someone else change my list?
text: Only if you share it with them as Can edit. They can then add, change and arrange what's in it, and what they delete goes to your Trash. People with Can view, and anyone with its link, can only look. Share a folder or list

heading: Can an AI agent delete my albums?
text: Not without you. An agent connected as Read-only can't change anything. With Manage collection, deleting waits until you approve it in Tonaris, and what's deleted stays in Trash for 30 days. Approve requests and manage connections

heading: Can I get back something deleted more than 30 days ago?
text: No. After 30 days in Trash, a folder, list or album is deleted for good, and nobody can bring it back. To keep a copy of everything, download your data now and then. Get something back from Trash

heading: Can I take my data with me?
text: Yes. On a computer, open Settings, then Data, and choose Download your data. You get a ZIP file with your whole collection, Trash included, readable by people and by programs. Tonaris can't read an export back in. Export your collection

heading: Can I use Tonaris on my phone?
text: Yes, in Safari or Chrome, and you can add it to your Home Screen. On a phone, you browse, search and open albums; adding and organizing need a computer. Tonaris on your phone

heading: Does Tonaris work without an internet connection?
text: No. If your connection drops, Tonaris keeps showing what it last loaded, and editing waits until you're back online. How saving works

heading: Is Tonaris in my language?
text: Tonaris itself is in English only for now. Your albums, lists and notes can be in any language, and keep their own spelling. Search finds names in other alphabets by their Latin spelling too: kino finds Кино. Search and commands

heading: Is there a light theme?
text: Not yet: Tonaris has a dark theme only. You can ask for a light theme, or vote for it, on the feedback board. Get in touch

text: Share ideas and report problems on the Tonaris feedback board. For a problem with your account, write to the support address. The feedback board is where you share ideas, report problems, and see what's planned. You sign in to it with your Tonaris account.

heading: Open the feedback board
text: Choose your name at the top of the sidebar. On a phone, tap your account button at the top right. Choose Feedback and ideas. Feedback and ideas opens the board in a new tab. The board opens in a new tab, at feedback.tonaris.app, and you arrive signed in. You need no other account.

heading: How the board works
text: It's public. Anyone can read it, but only Tonaris members can post, vote and comment. Vote before you post. Look for a post like yours first, and vote for it. Votes show what matters to the most people. Your name, not your email. The board shows your display name with what you post. It gets your email address too, to tell you about replies, but never shows it. See what's coming. When a request is taken up, its post is marked Planned, Started or Completed. Posts stay. What you post stays on the board if you delete your Tonaris account.

heading: Report a problem
text: A clear report helps fix a problem sooner. Say: what you did, step by step; what you expected, and what happened instead; any message Tonaris showed, word for word; your device and browser, such as "iPhone, Safari" or "Windows, Chrome". A screenshot helps too. The board is public. Leave out your email address, sign-in codes, and anything else private. If a change didn't save, When an edit doesn't save may already have the answer. Many questions are answered in Questions and answers.

heading: Problems with your account
text: For a problem you shouldn't post in public, such as losing access to your sign-in email, write to the support address on Lost access to your email?. Write from the address you use now, and say which address you sign in with.
